text: Snatch Game is a comedy challenge that has been a recurring feature across the Drag Race television franchise and is a central element of the reality competition series. Since the second season of the original American RuPaul's Drag Race in 2010, it has appeared in every subsequent season. Typically structured as a parody of Match Game (known as Blankety Blank in the UK, Blankety Blanks in Australia, and Jogo dos Pontinhos in Brazil), the challenge evaluates contestants' abilities in celebrity impersonation and improvisational comedy. It appears on various spin-offs, including All Stars and Secret Celebrity Drag Race, as well as international adaptations for Thai, British, Canadian, Dutch, Australian-New Zealand, Spanish, Italian, French, Philippine, Belgian, Swedish, Mexican, Brazilian, and German audiences. Usually held midway through each season, Snatch Game is widely regarded as one of the most significant and memorable challenges, with RuPaul stating it separates "the basic bitches from the fierce-ass queens." Winners of the show are often top performers in Snatch Game, though there are exceptions. Contestants typically impersonate women, though some choose male celebrities with flamboyant public images that align with a drag aesthetic. Several queens have impersonated individuals connected to the show, such as past or present contestants, Michelle Visage, or RuPaul. Queens cannot choose copyrighted characters, although some portrayals are based closely on specific screen performances. The challenge often features special celebrity guests who also serve as guest judges, though some episodes use the show’s regular production team—Michelle Visage, Ross Mathews, Carson Kressley, Rhys Nicholson, or members of the Pit Crew—instead. Ginger Minj has won Snatch Game three times, the most by any queen, while eight others have won it twice: BenDeLaCreme, Baga Chipz, Jinkx Monsoon, Trinity the Tuck, Jimbo, Hannah Conda, Gottmik, and Punani. Three queens—Gia Gunn, Onyx Unleashed, and Cynthia Lee Fontaine—have been eliminated twice due to their Snatch Game performances. Cristian Peralta won on the first season of Drag Race México by impersonating Verónica Castro; Luna Lansman won on the second season by impersonating José José. Xilhouete won on the first season of Drag Race Philippines by impersonating Vicki Belo; Captivating Katkat and Angel won on the second and third seasons by impersonating Joy Belmonte and Maria Clara, respectively. On Drag Race Philippines: Slaysian Royale, contestants performed a version called "Snatch Elections." Cardi B and Jennifer Coolidge are the most frequently impersonated celebrities; Coolidge was the first to be impersonated by two queens in the same Snatch Game, followed only by Liberace. Both queens who impersonated Mariah Carey and two of the five who impersonated Cardi B were eliminated, making these the only impersonations to result in multiple eliminations. Queens who impersonated Ariana Grande, Celine Dion, Ellen DeGeneres, Nancy Grace, and Rue McClanahan were up for elimination, as were two of the three who impersonated Lady Gaga, but only one queen was eliminated for each. Two of the four who impersonated Eartha Kitt and two of the three who impersonated Cher and RuPaul, respectively, landed in the bottom but were not eliminated. Three of the four who impersonated Liza Minnelli won the challenge, making her the first impersonation subject to earn multiple wins; Joan Rivers became the second after season 15. Snatch Game is considered the signature challenge on the show. Kevin O'Keeffe from Into notes that the challenge goes beyond impersonation, testing accuracy, humor, and character concept, as well as the queens' ability to shift from their signature look and be "funny on a dime." RuPaul consistently emphasizes that the cardinal rule is to make him laugh. Writing for Vulture, Bowen Yang and Matt Rogers call Snatch Game "the mother of all comedy challenges on a reality show," despite inconsistent results. However, Josh Lee of PopBuzz argues that while the challenge has delivered some of the show’s best moments, it has become stale, with recent impersonations lacking energy, and suggests the show should adapt or retire the challenge in future seasons.
